questions.q: What happens when a naphthalene ball is burnt in a metal plate in open space?
options: It burns with a blue flame.
It burns with yellow flame with no deposit on the metal plate.
It burns with a yellow flame with black soot deposited on the metal plate.
It burns with a blue flame with black soot deposited on the metal plate.
questions.explain: Naphthalene is an aromatic hydrocarbon. Due to its high carbon-to-hydrogen ratio, it undergoes incomplete combustion in the air, producing a yellow, sooty flame and depositing black soot.
questions.subject: General Science

questions.q: What happens when a zinc rod is placed in aqueous copper sulphate solution?
options: The blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.
The temperature of the solution falls.
Heat is required to start the reaction.
No chemical change observed.
questions.explain: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from the copper sulphate solution. This displacement reaction forms zinc sulphate, which is colourless, thus causing the blue colour of the solution to fade.

questions.q: The fractional atomic mass of chlorine is due to which of the following?
options: Presence of ions
Presence of isotopes
Its compound nature
Experimental error
questions.explain: Fractional atomic masses occur because most elements exist as a mixture of isotopes with different masses. The atomic mass is the weighted average of the isotopic masses.

questions.q: The functional group which does NOT contain oxygen hetero atom is:
options: halo alkane
ketone
carboxylic acid
alcohol
questions.explain: Haloalkanes contain halogen atoms (such as chlorine, fluorine, bromine, or iodine) as the hetero atom, not oxygen. Ketones, carboxylic acids, and alcohols all contain oxygen.

questions.q: What is the main role of micelles in the cleansing action of soap?
options: To trap and remove oil and dirt from clothes
To reduce the hardness of water
To produce lather with water
To increase the surface tension of water
questions.explain: Soap molecules form structures called micelles, where the hydrophobic ends attach to the oil and dirt particles, entrapping them in the center so they can be washed away in the water.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best explains the Law of Constant Proportions?
options: Elements are always found in random ratios in a compound.
Atoms can be divided into smaller particles during a reaction.
Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
A chemical compound always contains the same elements in the same proportion by mass.
questions.explain: The Law of Constant Proportions states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratio (by mass) and does not depend on its source and method of preparation.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT used for expressing the concentration of a solution?
options: Volume by Volume percentage of a solution
Volume by Mass percentage of a solution
Mass by volume percentage of a solution
Mass by mass percentage of a solution
questions.explain: Volume by mass percentage is generally not a standard unit for expressing concentration. Standard units include mass by mass (w/w), mass by volume (w/v), and volume by volume (v/v) percentage.

questions.q: Which of the following metals is extracted in the middle of the activity series?
options: Gold
Potassium
Iron
Sodium
questions.explain: Metals like iron, zinc, and lead fall in the middle of the reactivity series. They are moderately reactive and are typically extracted by reducing their oxides with carbon.
